newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks' short-term outlook stable - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks' short-term outlook stable - S&P.

text.p: The short-term outlook for Philippine banks remains stable in the face of increasing concerns over a possible property slump, a Standard & Poor's official said on Thursday.
However, Gavin Gunning, assistant executive director, told bankers they should be cautious in lending to the property sector to avoid the problems experienced recently by Thailand.
"The outlook is really quite stable here. The market is going through a very dynamic process of liberalisation and, as I've said before, that's linked with very strong economic growth."
Standard & Poor's have been in Manila for a week to undertake an annual review of nine Philippine banks.

He noted Philippine banking industry had experienced record lending growth in the past few years, which may result in problem loans if the property sector or economy experiences a downturn and if prudent lending policies are not adopted.
"Standard and Poor's does have concern that lending growth over the longer term might translate to into a high level of problematic (loans)," the official said.

So far, he said the ratio of past due loans plus foreclosed real estate assets as a percentage of total loans in the Philippines had not even reached 4.0 percent, while that of Thailand is seen peaking at 12 to 15 percent.
But he noted Philippine banks have become increasinly exposed to the property sector with loans to this sector comprising 27.2 percent of the total in 1995 compared with only 13.3 percent in 1992.
Banks have also been lending out more of their deposits with the proportion of loans to deposits reaching 100 percent for 14 Philippine banks under study.
However, loans comrpise 58 percent of their assets which is considered conservative in the international context, he said.
